chunks: Fadalah ibn 'Ukaym narrated from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Ziyad ibn Abi Raja', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him); and from Abu Sakhl, from Salman, who said:

I was sitting in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when a man came to him and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, [what is the ruling regarding] the slave?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'He has been tested by you and you have been tested by him, so that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, may see how grateful you are and how patient he is.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of slavery in Shia Islam as a test for both master and slave?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) frames the master-slave relationship not merely as a social or economic arrangement, but as a divine trial (ibtila') where both parties are observed for their spiritual conduct. It highlights the reciprocal nature of this test: the master is evaluated on his gratitude (shukr) for his status and his benevolence, while the slave is tested on his patience (sabr) in servitude. This perspective elevates domestic servitude to a sphere of worship and moral refinement within Shia ethical teachings.
